content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier-Customer Inventory Divergence", "construction": "For each firm, compute year-over-year change in inventory-to-sales ratio from quarterly Compustat (INVTQ/SALEQ). Using the FASB-mandated major customer disclosures (Compustat Segment Customer files), link each firm to its principal customers and compute the customer-weighted change in the customers' inventory-to-sales. The predictor is the firm's own inventory change minus its customers' inventory change, averaged over the trailing 4 quarters.", "rationale": "When a firm builds inventory while its downstream customers are drawing theirs down, it signals unanticipated demand weakness not yet impounded in the supplier's price, forecasting negative future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (customers building inventory faster than the firm)"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Momentum Acceleration", "construction": "Using Compustat annual order backlog (item OB) scaled by total assets, compute the change in backlog/assets from t-2 to t-1 minus the change from t-3 to t-2, i.e., the second difference (acceleration) of scaled backlog over three consecutive fiscal years.", "rationale": "Accelerating order backlog reflects an improving demand trajectory that investors underweight relative to level information, predicting higher subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (accelerating backlog)"}, {"name": "Intra-Firm Return Dispersion Across Segments", "construction": "For multi-segment firms, use Compustat Business Segment data to obtain each segment's SIC code. Assign each segment a value-weighted industry return over the trailing 12 months. Compute the sales-weighted standard deviation of these implied segment industry returns within the firm.", "rationale": "High dispersion in the fortunes of a firm's constituent businesses creates valuation complexity and limits-to-arbitrage, and diversified firms with wide segment-return dispersion tend to be undervalued, earning higher subsequent returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (wide cross-segment return dispersion)"}, {"name": "Deferred Revenue Growth Surprise", "construction": "Extract deferred/unearned revenue from Compustat (current DRC and long-term DRLT). Compute year-over-year growth in total deferred revenue scaled by lagged total assets, then take the residual from a cross-sectional regression on total sales growth. Rank on the residual.", "rationale": "Rising deferred revenue represents pre-paid future obligations and a leading indicator of subscription/contract demand not reflected in current recognized sales, forecasting higher future earnings and returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (positive deferred revenue growth surprise)"}, {"name": "Trading Volume Clustering at Round-Number Prices", "construction": "Using daily CRSP data over the trailing 6 months, compute the fraction of dollar trading volume occurring on days where the closing price is within 0.5% of a round dollar threshold (integer or 0.50 multiples), relative to total volume. Higher clustering indicates greater retail/noise-trader participation.", "rationale": "Stocks with heavy round-number volume clustering attract sentiment-driven noise traders, leading to overpricing that reverses, so high clustering predicts lower future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (little round-number clustering)"}, {"name": "Capitalized R&D-to-Market Momentum", "construction": "Build an R&D capital stock by accumulating Compustat XRD with a 20% annual depreciation rate over the prior 5 years. Scale this R&D capital by market equity. Interact by sorting: within the high R&D-capital-to-market group, further rank on trailing 6-month price momentum. The signal is the product of standardized R&D-capital/market and standardized momentum.", "rationale": "Innovation-intensive firms are hard to value; when high intangible intensity coincides with positive momentum, information about R&D payoffs is being gradually incorporated, predicting continued higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (high R&D intangibles combined with positive momentum)"}, {"name": "Analyst Coverage Change Relative to Peers", "construction": "Using I/B/E/S, count the number of analysts issuing FY1 estimates for each firm each month. Compute the 12-month change in coverage for the firm minus the median 12-month coverage change of its Fama-French 48-industry peers. Rank on the peer-adjusted change.", "rationale": "A relative increase in analyst coverage signals rising institutional interest and reduced information asymmetry ahead of good news, whereas relative coverage declines precede neglect and underperformance.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (rising coverage relative to peers)"}, {"name": "Working Capital Efficiency Trend", "construction": "Compute the cash conversion cycle (days receivable + days inventory - days payable) using Compustat quarterly items (RECTQ, INVTQ, APQ, SALEQ, COGSQ). Fit a linear trend to the trailing 8 quarters of the cash conversion cycle and use the negative of the slope (improving efficiency = shrinking cycle) as the signal.", "rationale": "A consistently shortening cash conversion cycle reflects improving operational efficiency and management quality that the market underappreciates, forecasting higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (steadily improving/shrinking cash conversion cycle)"}, {"name": "Idiosyncratic Volatility Asymmetry (Up vs Down Days)", "construction": "Using daily returns over the trailing 12 months, regress firm returns on the Fama-French three factors. Compute the residual standard deviation separately on days when the market return was positive versus negative. The signal is downside residual volatility minus upside residual volatility.", "rationale": "Stocks whose idiosyncratic risk concentrates on market-down days carry undesirable crash exposure and must offer higher expected returns as compensation.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (higher downside than upside idiosyncratic volatility)"}, {"name": "Pension Plan Asset Allocation Aggressiveness", "construction": "From Compustat pension footnote data, compute the expected long-term rate of return on plan assets (PPROR) and the equity allocation of plan assets. Rank firms on the residual of expected return regressed on funded status and firm size; high residuals indicate aggressive return assumptions.", "rationale": "Firms setting aggressive pension return assumptions inflate reported earnings and signal lower-quality accruals, leading to negative future return correction as reality falls short.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (conservative pension return assumptions)"}]}
